name: Probiotics
short: Trials have not shown increased risk, though safety reporting is weak. Rare bloodstream infections occur, mainly in people who are severely ill, immunosuppressed or in intensive care.
text: Safety reviews report that probiotic trials have shown no evidence of increased risk and that many controlled trials demonstrate safe use, but safety outcomes are inconsistently reported and an agency report found the literature not well equipped to answer safety questions with confidence. Rare cases of bacteraemia or fungaemia related to probiotic use have been described. Lactobacillus bacteraemia is infrequent but more common in people taking probiotics, and its risk factors include severe underlying disease, immune suppression, intensive care admission and central venous catheters; some probiotic strains have been matched to blood isolates. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
